newsitem.title: ITALY: Angola concerned about Zaire instability spreading.
newsitem.headline: Angola concerned about Zaire instability spreading.

text.p: Angola's President Jose Eduardo Dos Santos said on Saturday his country, concerned about instability on its large northern border with Zaire, supported the idea of sending a multinational force to eastern Zaire.

The 15-member U.N. Security Council on Friday unanimously approved the deployment of a Canadian-led multinational force until March 31 to ensure food and medicine reached hundreds of thousands of refugees in the Great Lakes area.

"We are now preoccupied with a recent threat to stability that is showing up on our northern border due to the conflict in eastern Zaire," Dos Santos told other heads of state and government leaders at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit.

"Angola supports the idea of creating a multinational force that can ensure that humanitarian aid is taken to the victims of the conflict and to avoid its expansion to other regions or even neighbouring countries."
Oil-exportor, Angola, which is also flanked by Zambia to the east, shares a large northern border with Zaire.

Dos Santos said Angola, devastated by war over the three decades since independence from Portugal, had increased its own agricultural production slightly this year but food imports and food aid were still essential to feed the population.
He said the government's goal was to move towards a market economy that stimulated private investment.

"To achieve these goals, big public and private investments for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the infrastructures of production will be necessary," he said. "For this the international community's and its foreign partners' assistance is urgent."
